subtype: Approach: alert friends and family to expect phishing [Action]
passage:
The leak had taken Jamal's contact list, and he knew his relatives in three countries would be next. On Saturday morning in Melbourne, before his tea went cold, he wrote in the family group: "My contacts were in a data leak. If a message comes from me or anyone asking for money, a code or a quick favour, please don't reply. Ring me instead."

Then he phoned his grandmother, who did not use the group, and read it to her slowly. He asked her to tell Aunty Sofia's household the same.

By noon his cousin Tuan wrote back, "Got a weird message from 'you' an hour ago. Ignored it. Good thing you warned us." Jamal felt his shoulders drop.

qa.q: Who did Jamal phone after posting in the family group?
qa.a: His grandmother, who did not use the group.

qa.q: What was Jamal feeling when Tuan's reply arrived?
qa.a: Jamal felt relieved, shown by his shoulders dropping when he learned the warning had come in time.

qa.q: What else could Jamal do for relatives who might still fall for a message, and why?
qa.a: Jamal could agree on a family code word to check that a request is really from him, because a shared check makes fake requests easy to spot.

qa.q: How might Tuan see the suspicious message once Jamal's warning arrived?
qa.a: Tuan probably felt confident to ignore it, since the warning made the strange message obviously suspect instead of confusing.

grounding: Because contact lists were part of the leak, the person tells relatives to ignore suspicious messages asking for money or codes.
